claims.text: The local row, Bulbapedia, and PokeBoon place the Can You Name All the Pokemon Neo? / Pokemon Ieru Ka Neo? CD route on June 28, 2000.
Bulbapedia identifies the single as a Pikachu Records release with catalogue numbers ZMDP-1084 and ZMVP-1104.

Bulbapedia describes the album as a four-track single-style album sung by Suzukisan and the Pokemon Kids, with Imakuni on the cover; its trivia notes that the album came with a Dance! Neo Imakuni? card.
The local source slice models one source-pinned card row for this route: Dance! Neo Imakuni? source index 164.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon credit Dance! Neo Imakuni? to Tomoaki Imakuni.

Bulbapedia identifies Tomoaki Imakuni as connected to Project Music and Project CharacterDex, and lists him across Pokemon music, TCG illustrator/personality cards, game credits, and TCG GB appearances.

This route matters because it makes a naming-song CD physically adjacent to a spoof Trainer card: the same Imakuni performance world appears in the album cover, the card identity, and the card's joke mechanics.

Bulbapedia says the card features the Pikachu Records logo in place of an expansion symbol, is one of several Japanese-exclusive spoof cards, has border text naming the Can You Name All the Pokemon Neo? extra card, and has HP 2000 with an arrow pointing to it saying lie.
Bulbapedia's card text says the player chooses Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned for their Active Pokemon, and that Imakuni? cannot be played as a Pokemon.

Agents should keep this Dance! Neo Imakuni? CD route separate from the 1997 glossy CoroCoro Imakuni?, the 1999 Tropical Mega Battle non-glossy Imakuni?, Expansion Sheet 3 Imakuni? special rows, Trade Please!, Shining Imakuni?, later Supporter reprints, and CD-only listings where the card has been removed.

The catalog can make the CD route, Pikachu Records symbol, spoof-card features, and Imakuni credit legible, but it does not prove seller possession, authenticity, condition, price, unopened CD integrity, card presence inside a CD lot, or spendability.

narrative.human_title: Can You Name All the Pokemon Neo? — when the song brings its own card
narrative.why_it_matters: This is Pokemon media behaving like a pocket circus. The CD asks children to name the new Pokemon, Imakuni stares out from the cover, Pikachu Records stamps the card where an expansion symbol should be, and the insert card turns the whole thing into a joke Trainer with impossible HP and status-condition chaos. Dance! Neo Imakuni? is not important because it is tidy. It is important because it refuses to be tidy: music, performance, parody, and cardboard all arrive in the same little package.

card_highlights.why_it_matters: Dance! Neo Imakuni? is a tiny historical grin. It is a card that knows the singer, the CD, and the joke are all part of the same machine. The fake HP, the status-condition chaos, the Pikachu Records mark, and the real-person Imakuni image make it a perfect test of whether an agent can preserve playfulness without turning it into a sloppy match.

narrative.human_title: Dance! Neo Imakuni? — the CD promo that refuses to behave
narrative.why_it_matters: This card is a little performance artifact dressed as a Trainer card. HP 2000, except the card itself says that is a lie. Status chaos, except it is also a joke about Imakuni not being a Pokemon. Pikachu Records where a set symbol ought to be. It is exactly why the catalog cannot be only names and prices. The route is the meaning: a Johto naming song, a CD insert, a performer on the cover, and a card that turns all of that into cardboard.
